body.estimand_functional: For sequences in the outcome-inference subclass \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PSRR}}\), along even \(n\ge N_0\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n)\Rightarrow b^{\mathsf T}C_{k,a}+s\varepsilon\), with \(\widehat\tau_n\) the terminal observed-arm difference in means; the outcome-free covariate-design class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PSRR}}^x\) carries only the allocation-path, runtime, and clipped-covariate conclusions.

sampling_model.design: Original Zhu--Liu equal-allocation PSRR: uniform balanced initialization, treated--control pair proposals, Metropolis acceptance \(\min\{1,(M/M^*)^{\gamma}\}\), and immediate first entry into \(M\le a\).
sampling_model.units: For allocation and endpoint results, the primitive object is a deterministic bounded covariate triangular array with fixed \(k\), convergent covariate second moments, and uniformly positive-definite covariance. For joint residual and causal-inference results, this is restricted to a subclass with fixed potential outcomes, no interference, bounded and convergent outcome second moments, and nondegenerate outcome-sum projection residual variance. Assignment is the only randomness. Each scope discards only the finitely many rows before its own regular tail.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly \(n/2\) units receive treatment and \(n/2\) receive control; there is no interference and one version of each treatment.
sampling_model.overlap: Equal allocation gives design probabilities \(1/2\) by label-complement symmetry; no superpopulation propensity is used.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Terminal treated- and control-arm OLS projection moments estimate \(b_n\) and the conservative residual envelope \(u_n\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The authors state that it is challenging to derive the asymptotic distribution of commonly used test statistics and leave it to future work.
The estimator has a linear combination of a Gaussian random variable and truncated Gaussian random variables as its asymptotic distribution.
The stationary mass is proportional to a negative power of Mahalanobis imbalance, and a later accept--reject correction restores uniformity.
Under uniform Mahalanobis rerandomization, an estimated Gaussian-plus-truncated-Gaussian law gives conservative intervals under heterogeneous effects.
The fully interacted estimator is asymptotically most efficient and permits inference identical to complete randomization under the studied p-value designs.
A sample-based Gaussian push-forward yields asymptotically conservative weak-null inference for a broad class of rerandomized designs.
A speeded component of random-walk Metropolis converges weakly to the appropriate Langevin diffusion.
Finite-population random-partition statistics satisfy vector central limit theorems under covariance and maximal-term regularity.
The fully interacted OLS estimator is asymptotically normal and its Huber--White variance is conservative under complete randomization.
A closed-form covariate-adjusted confidence interval is obtained by inverting Fisher randomization tests, with an observed-data sufficient condition for correct randomization-based coverage.

body.tldr: Original equal-allocation first-entry PSRR has an outcome-free allocation limit on a regular bounded covariate-design class: the proposal-time chain converges to an exterior radial diffusion, its first-entry time has an explicit Tricomi-\(U\) Laplace transform, and its all-proposal count exceeds its accepted-switch count by only \(O_{\Pr}(\sqrt n)\). The terminal imbalance is a radially clipped Gaussian, independent of a stationary Gaussian outcome-residual coordinate on the smaller outcome-inference subclass. Fixed finite tuning changes the search-time law but not the first-order endpoint law. On the outcome subclass, stopped-arm moments consistently estimate the inputs to a computable variance-envelope interval for the finite-population ATE, with the stated fully interacted corollary.

project_justification.gap: Zhu and Liu leave asymptotic distributions of common statistics under original first-entry PSRR open. Uniform rerandomization instead conditions a Gaussian inside the balance region, while Lu, Zhang, and Zhu analyze a stationary chain and add a correction; neither supplies the proposal-time first-entry law, its runtime transform, or weak-null ATE inference for the original output.
project_justification.niche: The paper isolates two nested scopes: an outcome-free regular covariate-design class for the allocation path, runtime, clipped endpoint, and boundary-atom converse, and an outcome-inference subclass for the residual process, stopped moments, and finite-population causal intervals.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives actual-filtration predictable characteristics by a uniform-shadow coupling and antisymmetric-score cancellation, proves compact containment and martingale-problem convergence, transfers the first hit, and globalizes the fixed-horizon rejection bound to show that the all-proposal clock exceeds the accepted-switch clock by \(O_{\Pr}(\sqrt n)\). It solves the radial hitting ODE in Tricomi-\(U\) form and then obtains the independent residual limit and downstream variance-envelope inference without assuming projected Markovianity, stabilization, or finite-population outcome--residual independence.

body.related_work: Zhu and Liu define the original equal-allocation, immediate-stop PSRR algorithm and leave asymptotic distributions of commonly used statistics open; the two-class functional theorem closes that gap on a bounded regular covariate subclass and shows more sharply that their accepted-switch state index differs from the present all-proposal count by \(O_{\Pr}(\sqrt n)\), hence by \(o_{\Pr}(n)\). Lu, Zhang, and Zhu derive a negative-power stationary law and restore uniformity through an additional correction, whereas the present result keeps the original first-entry output and obtains a tuning-indexed Tricomi-\(U\) runtime transform. Li, Ding, and Rubin derive the Gaussian-plus-truncated-Gaussian law for uniform Mahalanobis rerandomization; the outcome-free boundary atom here proves that original first-entry PSRR has a different terminal law, and this non-representation certificate transfers to the broader published algorithmic class by subclass inclusion even though the positive diffusion theorem remains on the regular subclass. Roberts, Gelman, and Gilks motivate the diffusion scaling, and Li and Ding supply the finite-population Gaussian initialization substrate. Li and Ding's regression-adjustment theory, Lin's fully interacted linearization, Zhao and Ding's cancellation result, Cohen and Fogarty's Gaussian push-forward, and Fiksel's Fisher-exact inversion remain distinct inference comparators to the outcome-subclass variance-envelope analysis.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The six-row zero-correlation witness proves that the Metropolis-kink drift cannot be controlled uniformly over arbitrary balanced states: zero projected scores and zero covariate--residual covariance do not force the antisymmetric pair average to vanish. The proved characteristic result is therefore deliberately localized along the actual uniformly initialized path, where the all-pairs coupling and arm empirical concentration give the needed cancellation. Characteristics are used only before entry, where \(M_n>a>0\); the terminal crossing is handled by its exact vanishing transposition increment. This resolves the earlier kill test without adding an empirical-distribution limit or initialization assumption, but it does not create a uniform-over-states generator theorem.
body.honest_scope: The allocation-path, proposal-clock, runtime-transform, clipped-endpoint, and boundary-atom results hold on a regular outcome-free covariate-design subclass of original Zhu--Liu equal-allocation PSRR. The joint stationary residual coordinate and all ATE, stopped-moment, variance-envelope, and fully interacted conclusions hold only on the nested outcome-inference subclass with fixed bounded potential outcomes and nondegenerate projection-residual variance. Zhu--Liu's published state index counts accepted switches, whereas \(T_n^x\) here counts every proposal; the difference is \(O_{\Pr}(\sqrt n)\), so the clocks are first-order equivalent, but no limiting rejection-count constant or distribution is claimed. The limiting hitting-time law is computable through its Tricomi-\(U\) Laplace transform; no convergence of finite-chain expected runtime is claimed. The proof is complete for the actual-path characteristics, compact containment, martingale problem, random-clock conversion, and continuous first-hit transfer. It assumes fixed \(k\), fixed \(a>0\), fixed finite \(\gamma\), equal arms, bounded leverage, and sequencewise asymptotics. It excludes shrinking thresholds, growing dimension, divergent tuning, unequal arms, sequential enrollment, stationary or rejection-corrected variants, uniform approximation rates, superpopulation claims, and finite-sample exactness. The positive diffusion theorem does not extend beyond the regular subclass; only the logical refutation of a universal uniform-acceptable-set representation transfers to the broader published class by subclass inclusion.
